approved: Commonwealth Electoral Amendment (Lowering Voting Age and Increasing Voter Participation) Bill 2018
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would let 16- and 17-year-olds vote in federal elections.
Eligible Australians who are not enrolled could sign up and vote on the day at a polling centre.
A 14- or 15-year-old could be placed on the electoral roll ahead of turning 16.
Lower the voting age to 16 while keeping compulsory voting and candidacy at 18.
Allow 14- and 15-year-olds to be registered on the electoral roll in advance.
Permit unenrolled voters to enrol and cast a provisional vote at a polling place on election day.
Australians aged 16 and 17, and eligible voters who are not enrolled or have the wrong address.
